title: GIANTSAN: Efficient Memory Sanitization with Segment Folding
problem: Location-based memory sanitization methods suffer from low protection density, where each metadata element guards a limited number of bytes, requiring excessive metadata loading for numerous memory accesses and creating high runtime overhead.
motivation: Efficient memory error detection is essential for production systems, but existing sanitizers impose prohibitive performance penalties that hinder adoption.
method: GIANTSAN uses segment folding to increase the protection density of memory metadata by logically folding multiple memory segments into fewer metadata entries. This reduces the frequency of metadata loads during runtime while preserving the high compatibility of location-based approaches through careful bookkeeping of folded regions.
key_novelty: Segment folding as a mechanism to increase metadata protection density and reduce runtime metadata loading overhead without sacrificing detection accuracy.
contributions: Identifies low protection density as a fundamental bottleneck in location-based memory sanitizers
Introduces segment folding technique to increase effective protection density
Demonstrates substantial runtime overhead reduction over baseline sanitizers like ASan

metrics.speedup: Significant overhead reduction over baseline sanitizers
metrics.accuracy: Maintains detection accuracy of baseline methods

limitations: Paper does not discuss limitations or scenarios where segment folding may reduce detection capability.
primary_theme: Efficient memory safety through segment folding
